clue.text: No ruddy pioneer in Indian country

definitions.text: No ruddy pioneer in Indian country

parts.words: No ruddy pioneer in Indian country
parts.note: a settler who is not ruddy-cheeked has a pallid complexion, and that is what Native Americans in westerns called the white newcomers

explanation.surface: A sickly-looking frontiersman pushes into the American West.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Indian' here means Native American, not someone from India: the whole clue describes a white settler of the Old West, a face that is not ruddy.
explanation.definitionFit: In westerns, Native Americans' name for a white settler refers to their pallid complexion.

clue.text: One gets tossed in Spain chancy business

parts.words: One gets tossed in Spain chancy business
parts.note: a coin is tossed when settling something by chance, and this was the coin used in Spain before the euro

explanation.surface: Someone in Spain is thrown about in a risky venture.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue describes the old Spanish coin: it is what gets tossed, heads or tails, in the chancy business of a coin toss.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the Spanish unit of currency, a coin that could be flipped, before the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: The old tomato's got nothing on Granny Smith

parts.note: love is zero, nothing, in tennis scoring
a Granny Smith is a variety of green apple

explanation.surface: An elderly lady named Granny Smith outdoes an old tomato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Granny Smith' reads as a person, but it is the green apple variety. 'on' simply joins the two pieces in a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: This was an old English name for the tomato, once thought to be an aphrodisiac.

clue.text: Sound of trumpets — or maybe popcorn for the aficionado ?

parts.note: an aficionado is a fan or devotee
popcorn is an example of fare, food

explanation.surface: A cinema enthusiast's snack is compared to a blast of trumpets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'popcorn for the aficionado' is the fan's fare, read in answer order as FAN then FARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A flourish played on brass instruments to herald an arrival or announcement.

clue.text: American Indian student takes the catch

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people of Canada
L is for learner, a student driver's plate

explanation.surface: A Native American student makes a catch.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is by association: the wicker basket an angler keeps fish in holds the catch. 'takes' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: An angler's wicker basket holds the fish that have been caught.

clue.text: Reaction to terror that's frightfully funny

definitions.meaning: colloquially, something hilarious is called this

explanation.surface: Someone describes a horror film that is so bad it's hilarious.
explanation.definitionFit: A shriek is the natural response to fright, and in colloquial British speech a hilarious person or event is also called by this name.

clue.text: Was this palace set to receive 2LO ?

definitions.text: Was this palace set to receive 2LO ?

parts.words: Was this palace set to receive 2LO
parts.note: a famous London glass exhibition palace, and an early radio receiver called a set, which picked up 2LO, the BBC's first London station

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a palace was equipped to pick up an early radio station.
explanation.walkthrough: The word fits both 'palace' (the London glass exhibition building of 1851) and 'set' (an early radio built round a mineral detector); 2LO was the BBC's original London station of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1851 London exhibition building was named for its glass, and early radio receivers using a mineral detector bore the same name.

clue.text: French spa's artless uprising

indicators.note: in a down clue an uprising means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: naive means artless, innocent

explanation.surface: A rebellion breaks out naively at a French resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' reverses NAIVE in this down clue to give the spa town.
explanation.definitionFit: A town on Lake Geneva in France famous for its bottled mineral water.

clue.text: As one maybe, having some haziness over a sphere of knowledge

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the haze piece on top of the rest

parts.note: mist is a light haziness
one's ken is one's range of knowledge

explanation.surface: A muddled thinker's view of a field of learning is clouded.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone can be in error; to be wrong is how one may be.

clue.text: Rider gets a little publicity with Crazy Edmund

parts.note: an ad, a short advertisement, is a little publicity

indicators.note: crazy signals the letters of the name are jumbled

explanation.surface: A jockey gets some press coverage alongside a wild man called Edmund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rider' is not a horseman but a clause added to a document. 'Crazy' rearranges EDMUND into DENDUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is an extra clause added to a legal document, an appendix.

clue.text: I'll be damned if I try one a day for a week !

definitions.text: I'll be damned if I try one a day for a week !

parts.words: I'll be damned if I try one a day for a week
parts.note: seven days, one each day, of the mortal faults in Christian teaching that lead to damnation

explanation.surface: Someone flatly refuses a week-long regime, one item each day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I'll be damned' reads as a mild oath of refusal, but taken literally it is what committing these would bring about: there are seven of them, one per day of the week.
explanation.definitionFit: Christian moral teaching lists seven mortal faults (pride, greed, lust, envy, gluttony, wrath, sloth) that lead to damnation.

clue.text: Right returned benefit to Labour ?

indicators.note: returned means the abbreviation for right is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: to avail is to be of benefit; as a noun, avail is benefit or use

explanation.surface: A right-winger reverts and offers a handout to the Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like Britain's Labour Party, but it is the definition in its sense of toil. 'returned' turns RT into TR.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean painful, exhausting work or toil, and both are also used of childbirth.

clue.text: From Los Angeles to Niagara a Socialist republic

indicators.note: the letters are taken from inside the run of words that follows, spanning the place names

explanation.surface: A trip across America from Los Angeles to Niagara Falls passes a socialist state.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in angelES TO NIAgara. The clue dates from when this Baltic country was a Soviet Socialist Republic.
explanation.definitionFit: This Baltic state was a Soviet Socialist Republic within the USSR from 1940 until 1991.

clue.text: Like the vision attending Wordsworth's youth

definitions.text: Like the vision attending Wordsworth's youth

parts.words: Like the vision attending Wordsworth's youth
parts.note: a quotation from Wordsworth's Intimations Ode, where the youth 'by the vision ... is on his way attended'

explanation.surface: A description of the poet William Wordsworth's inspiration as a young man.
explanation.walkthrough: Wordsworth's Ode: Intimations of Immortality says the youth 'by the vision splendid / Is on his way attended'; the clue asks for the missing adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Wordsworth's poem describes that youthful vision as magnificent with this very adjective.

clue.text: Money a mad fellow put on a tea-table

parts.note: dough is slang for money
a nut is a crazy person

explanation.surface: A madman spends his cash on a tea table.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description: a ring of fried dough is something set out on a tea-table.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet fried cake, often ring-shaped, served at teatime.

clue.text: But some would call such living" fast"

definitions.text: But some would call such living" fast"

parts.words: But some would call such living" fast
parts.note: a dissolute way of life is described as fast living or by another adjective meaning unrestrained

explanation.surface: Some people describe a racy lifestyle as fast.
explanation.walkthrough: Both adjectives describe a dissolute life: fast living and its near-synonym, which also means slack or free.
explanation.definitionFit: A life of sexual or moral laxity is called fast or dissolute, unrestrained living.

clue.text: Functioning as a factory hand

explanation.surface: A man works on the factory floor.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means in effect or working; as a noun it is a mill or factory worker.

clue.text: The roe of this fish is generally unappreciated

definitions.text: The roe of this fish is generally unappreciated

parts.words: The roe of this fish is generally unappreciated
parts.note: alludes to Hamlet's 'caviare to the general', something too fine for ordinary people; caviar is this fish's roe

explanation.surface: A remark that most people don't care for a certain fish's eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'generally' alludes to Hamlet's 'caviare to the general': a delicacy lost on ordinary people. Caviar is the roe of this large fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Caviar, the costly delicacy, is the salted roe of this large fish.

clue.text: Harris's flower ?

parts.note: Harris cloth is a famous woollen fabric from the Hebrides, and a flower in crosswords is something that flows, a river

explanation.surface: Someone asks which flower is Harris's favourite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is read as 'one that flows', a river, here the river on the Scottish border; Harris is the Hebridean island whose woven woollen cloth bears the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish border river shares its name with the rough woollen cloth woven on the isle of Harris.

clue.text: Gerontius finds me in gloomy surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the word for gloomy is placed around the other piece

parts.note: drear is a poetic word for gloomy
taken as written

explanation.surface: Gerontius discovers me in a dismal place.
explanation.walkthrough: Elgar's oratorio The Dream of Gerontius makes Gerontius the one who dreams; 'in' is a link and 'surroundings' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Elgar's oratorio is The Dream of Gerontius, so its central figure is the one having the vision.

clue.text: Revealed as a villain-or as a gatecrasher if Monsieur left

indicators.note: left means Monsieur's letter is left in place within the other word, so the two combine

parts.note: a gatecrasher arrives without an invitation, uninvited

explanation.surface: A masked-ball intruder is exposed as the villain of the piece.
explanation.walkthrough: Leave M (Monsieur) in UNASKED, a gatecrasher's state, and the result is the answer; take the M out and it is UNASKED again. At a masked ball, both words fit the intruder.
explanation.definitionFit: A villain whose disguise is pulled off is exposed, shown for what they are.

clue.text: A custom in South Africa to get a skinful

parts.note: usage is custom, habitual practice

explanation.surface: A South African tradition involves getting thoroughly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a skinful' suggests too much to drink, but it is a casing filled with minced meat.
explanation.definitionFit: A banger is minced meat packed into a casing, literally a skin filled up.

clue.text: Wrote in confinement

definitions.meaning: put down in writing with a pen
shut up in an enclosure or pen

explanation.surface: Someone wrote while locked up in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the past tense of writing with a pen, and also means shut in a fold or enclosure.

clue.text: How Lady Bountiful might treat her serf perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the letters of these words may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A generous lady of the manor looks after her servant.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Bountiful, from Farquhar's play The Beaux' Stratagem, is the type of the charitable lady of the manor; 'perhaps' rearranges HER SERF.
explanation.definitionFit: A charitable hostess revives a tired servant with food and drink, restoring their energy.

clue.text: Winning service within a foot of the stone surface

indicators.note: within means the serve word is placed inside the abbreviation

parts.note: FT is the abbreviation for a foot
an ace is a serve in tennis that wins the point outright

explanation.surface: A winning tennis serve lands within a foot of a stone surface.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Winning service' is tennis, not gem-cutting; 'within' is the container signal and 'of' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: One of the flat polished faces cut on a gemstone.

clue.text: A holy war with no refinements, about sex appeal

indicators.note: about means the word for unrefined goes around the abbreviation

parts.note: something crude has no refinements

explanation.surface: A holy war is waged crudely over matters of sexual allure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex appeal' reads as part of the surface's argument, but it is just its abbreviation, which 'about' wraps the crude word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval Christian military expedition to recover the Holy Land, hence any war fought for religion.

clue.text: Backbone feature, note

parts.note: the chin is a facial feature
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A feature of the backbone is noted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' reads as a characteristic of the backbone, but it is a feature of the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A cut of meat containing the spine, and the anatomical term for the backbone itself.

clue.text: Late message for a heretic ?

parts.note: ex- means former, late
a communication is a message

explanation.surface: A belated notice is sent to someone guilty of heresy.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines and builds the answer: the church's message to a heretic is one that makes them a 'late' communicant, cast out of communion.
explanation.definitionFit: The church formally cuts a heretic off from communion and membership of the church.

clue.text: Dame in such a state after the strip-tease!

definitions.text: Dame in such a state after the strip-tease!

parts.words: Dame in such a state after the strip-tease
parts.note: the personified Mother of the natural world is called Dame, and a stripper ends up naked, in a state of her

explanation.surface: A lady finds herself in quite a state once the striptease is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dame' is the personified mother of the natural world, and 'in a state of' her is the idiom for being naked, as a stripper is when the act ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The personified natural world is 'Dame' or 'Mother', and the idiom for naked is 'in a state of' this.

clue.text: Like the parson, never worried when in debt

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside the other, here the word for debt

parts.note: to be in the red is to be in debt

indicators.note: worried means these letters are agitated into another order

explanation.surface: A vicar who stays calm even when he owes money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' gives VEREN from never, and 'in' places it inside the word for debt, splitting it after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman is addressed or described by this title of respect, used as an adjective for clergy.
